items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names explain themselves (ConsistentHashHeader, mergeConsistentHashPolicies, constructConsistentHash). API types have doc comments, merge branches carry priority comments such as "// p2 has higher priority (e.g., PreferParent)", and the code follows the existing plugin style.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Wired in like the other features (IR field, Equals, Validate, apply, merge func). But mergeConsistentHashPolicies spans about 80 lines (consistent_hash.go L273-L353), and mergeConsistentHash repeats the same clone+SetOne body in two back-to-back disable branches.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: MinLength=1 is set on the key fields, constructConsistentHash errors are appended in ConstructIR, a Validate() hook is registered, and unsupported merge strategies log a warning instead of failing silently. Deep clone avoids sharing IR state between routes.

items.name: Multi-policy merge semantics
items.evidence: mergeConsistentHash is registered in MergeTrafficPolicies. It handles both strategy families, orders inputs as mergeConsistentHashPolicies(higher, lower) for union, dedup and re-sort, honours disable, and records "consistentHash" via mergeOrigins.SetOne/Append. Hidden tests pass.

items.name: Empty spec and disable handling
items.name_zh: 空配置与 disable 处理
items.evidence: The CEL rule "!has(self.disable) || !self.disable || (!has(self.headers)...)" appears in the generated CRD YAML. Empty {} defaults to a single sourceIp policy with terminal=false. The merge test shows disable suppresses an inherited parent policy and HashPolicy is nil.
